picked.t: Company of Southeast Asia’s richest man posts first $1B quarterly profit
picked.body: Vietnam’s largest listed company saw revenue almost quadruple year-on-year to VND150.58 trillion, according to the company’s financial report. As in the first two quarters, real estate generated the largest share of revenue, at nearly VND98.5 trillion, or more than 65% of the total. By September-end, Vingroup held nearly VND107 trillion in cash and bank deposits. During the period, it also raised about $2.3 billion through bond issuance, the sale of preferred shares and syndicated loans from international investors. Since 2025, Vingroup has expanded into power and infrastructure, alongside traditional businesses including real estate, industrial manufacturing and technology. Real estate, however, remains the main growth driver for the conglomerate led by billionaire Vuong. VNDirect Securities estimates that real estate will remain Vingroup’s mainstay, contributing at least 50% of its total revenue and profit over the next five years. Meanwhile, its electric vehicle, infrastructure and energy businesses are expected to expand rapidly, raising their combined share of the group’s revenue to 30%–40% over the long term. This year, Vuong’s conglomerate is developing a series of major projects across the country. In real estate, it is building several urban areas spanning thousands of hectares, including projects in Quang Ninh, Hanoi and HCMC. In infrastructure, Vingroup, through its subsidiaries, is involved in engineering, procurement and construction contracts for five urban railway lines in Hanoi, with a total value of about $49 billion. Vuong, chairman of Vingroup, is the richest man in Southeast Asia with $37.7 billion in net worth, according to real-time data by Forbes.

picked.t: Vietnam lowers electricity price, first time in almost 20 years
picked.body: Average retail price is now at VND2,159.90 per kilowatt-hour, according to the Vietnam Electricity. This is the first decrease in the average electricity price in nearly 20 years, excluding five rounds of reductions in electricity bills and prices to support people and businesses affected by Covid-19. Between 2023 and 2025, electricity prices rose by 18.2% in four adjustments. The last increase was made in May 2025. Before those increases, electricity prices had remained unchanged for more than four years, from March 2019 to May 2023. EVN said the reduction followed a review of its operations and efforts to calculate and cut costs as much as possible. The adjustment is intended to support people and businesses, help stabilize the macroeconomy and ensure social welfare. At a National Assembly session on economic and social issues on the morning of Oct. 31, Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang said the government had directed EVN to cut costs as much as possible to lower average retail electricity prices by about 2%. He said the electricity price reduction, together with a plan to cut the special consumption tax on gasoline to zero, would provide about 0.07 percentage points of additional room to control inflation and work toward the 4.5% target set by the National Assembly.
